diagnostic.answer: A complete answer should name the problem it solves, the values or control flow involved, and one mistake to avoid.

sections.title: Objects model named data
sections.body: An object groups properties under keys. Object literals are useful for records such as a user, product, or configuration. A property can hold any value, including another object or a function. Choose names that describe the domain rather than the current screen position.

sections.title: Read and write properties
sections.body: Dot access is clear for a known valid identifier: user.name. Bracket access evaluates an expression and is required for dynamic keys or keys with spaces: user[field]. Reading a missing property returns undefined; following another property from that undefined value throws unless you check it.

sections.title: Methods are function properties
sections.body: A method is a function stored in a property. In account.deposit(), normal method syntax can read this as account because of the call form. If the method is detached and called alone, that connection is lost. Prefer explicit parameters when shared behavior does not need receiver state.

sections.title: Keys, values, and entries
sections.body: Object.keys returns own enumerable string keys, Object.values returns values, and Object.entries returns key-value pairs. These produce arrays and can be mapped or filtered. Do not use for...in blindly when inherited enumerable properties would be a problem.

sections.title: Why this matters in React
sections.body: Objects and property access is part of the JavaScript model React code already uses. Components, event handlers, state updates, list rendering, and data requests become easier to reason about when this concept is understood without framework shortcuts. Practise the JavaScript behavior first, then identify the same rule in JSX or a component.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain objects and property access to a junior developer.
interviewQuestions.answer: Use objects to group named values. Choose dot or bracket property access. Understand methods and this at call time. Iterate own object data safely.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Show a small example and one common mistake.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you prove that code using objects and property access behaves correctly?
interviewQuestions.answer: State the expected value or control flow first, test normal and boundary cases, and inspect the actual runtime result. Explain the JavaScript rule behind the evidence.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which edge case would you test first?

interviewQuestions.question: Where can objects and property access affect React code?
interviewQuestions.answer: It can affect values, callbacks, rendering decisions, updates, or data flow. The exact connection depends on the concept; the important step is to reason from JavaScript behavior before blaming React.

commonMistakes.symptom: Code using objects and property access produces a surprising value.
commonMistakes.cause: The result was run before the value, type, scope, identity, or control flow was predicted.
commonMistakes.fix: Reduce the case, write the expected result, and apply the exact rule from the matching section.

commonMistakes.symptom: A learner copies syntax but cannot adapt it.
commonMistakes.cause: The example was memorized without explaining why it works.
commonMistakes.fix: Change the data and names, predict again, and explain which behavior must stay the same.

commonMistakes.symptom: A React problem is blamed on React immediately.
commonMistakes.cause: The underlying JavaScript behavior was not isolated first.
commonMistakes.fix: Reproduce the value or function behavior in a small JavaScript example, then reconnect it to the component.
